title: The AI industry is booming. Women are getting left behind
key_facts: LinkedIn report: women were about a quarter of new hires in AI roles in the past year versus 50% in non-AI roles.
In executive roles the share drops to 13%.
Women are more likely to work in roles with high AI-disruption exposure, such as customer service.
AI job postings have doubled since 2023 and pay more than twice as much on average as non-AI roles.
Men's median pay across AI occupations is $45,000 higher than women's.
Women are concentrated in lower-paid AI roles such as data annotators.
Women hold about one-third of US tech jobs.
quote_evidence: "AI is creating some of the fastest growing, highest paying and most consequential jobs in the global economy," said LinkedIn's Sarah Steinberg.
"What we're witnessing is a sort of backsliding," said AnitaB.org president Brenda Darden Wilkerson.
why_it_matters_hint: Women are under-represented in the best-paid new AI jobs and over-represented in exposed ones.
notes: Based on a recent LinkedIn report; advocates' views quoted.
